WIN-HGO-S-20261009 report (goldfish-deep, Sonnet 5.5 / xhigh). CLOSING-ALLOWANCE / 80 % CHECKPOINT HANDOVER: partial. Slices S2 and S4 are implemented and committed; S1 and S3 are NOT done. Implementation partial, independent review: pending, PO acceptance pending.

Route pre-check: class is test-only (QG-04), not A/G/S. Requested route: goldfish-deep, Sonnet 5.5 / xhigh, tool-layer model sonnet. Observed (this dispatch's runtime prompt): "Sonnet 5.5 ... claude-sonnet-5-5". No contradiction. GUARD-BOOTSTRAP-RECEIPT-MISSING fired once on the first Write; the named preflight ran once (exit 0), then the write succeeded.

Closing-allowance handover (pipeline.dispatch-closing-allowance.v1)
1. Committed: 89faa3fb7 "test(human-guard-override): make the win32 cases measure the product, not the host" (SHA from my own commit output): S2 (three killed-writer helpers) and S4 (held-lock case), in plugins/pipeline-core/lib/human-guard-override.test.mjs only. Nothing else committed.
2. Verified green: see section 2. Native: 10 of 11 targeted cases pass; WSL: the same 11 patterns, wrapped exit 0.
3. Remains undone: S1 (symlink gate, 4 cases); S3 (NVA-HGOFIX-2 x3, the script-file backslash case, CROSSREPOGUIDANCE-1a/1b); one further native red in the S2 chunk (below). No tracked file is left modified or uncommitted.
4. Next briefing adjustments: see section 6.

1. DoD results
- S2 killed-writer helper injects the win32 private-state assurance and does not assert SIGKILL on win32: passed natively (the 10 killed-writer cases that reached the helper assertion are green except the one below).
- S4 held-lock case accepts HGO-AUDIT-LOCK-AMBIGUOUS on win32 and still asserts the lock survives: passed natively (case "a failed repair or ordinary append never removes the active repair writer's lock").
- S1 symlink cases gated on the shared probe: NOT DONE (no edit made).
- S3 NVA-HGOFIX-2 explicit platform, backslash-filename fixture typed skip, CROSSREPOGUIDANCE normalisation: NOT DONE (no edit made).
- Per-chunk native captures showing the targeted cases green: partial. One chunk captured; 10 pass, 1 fail. No chunk exists for S1/S3.
- WSL capture of the same chunk showing no change: passed (wrapped exit 0; I did not read the artifact's counts).
- One commit with the prescribed subject: passed for the slices landed (89faa3fb7).

2. Evidence (repo-root-relative; evidence/ is git-ignored)
- evidence/WIN-HGO-S-20261009/chunk-1-lib-killed-writer-and-held-lock.txt: node plugins/pipeline-core/scripts/capture-evidence.mjs --label WIN-HGO-S-chunk-1 --out <that path> -- node --test --test-name-pattern=<11 name patterns> plugins/pipeline-core/lib/human-guard-override.test.mjs ; native Windows ; wrapped exit 1 ; ℹ pass 10, ℹ fail 1.
- evidence/WIN-HGO-S-20261009/wsl-chunk-1-lib-killed-writer-and-held-lock.txt: the same command run under WSL via wsl.exe -e bash -lc "cd <repo-root-in-wsl>; ..." ; wrapped exit 0.
- The one native red: "a recovery guard excludes a second reclaimer and a raced replacement is never unlinked" (test at lib test line 2579 after my edit; afterRecoveryGuardFn at 2590 re-enters acquireAuditLock). It throws HumanGuardOverrideError "audit lock recovery owner state is ambiguous", raised at human-guard-override.mjs:2527 (clearAbandonedAuditRecovery, called from acquireAuditLock at :2545). Same root cause as S4: the recovery guard is held by this very live process and win32 has no "live" owner answer by documented design. I did NOT read this test's assertions, so "test fault, not product fault" is a strong hypothesis, not a confirmed verdict. Before my change this case died earlier, at the helper's SIGKILL assertion.

3. Changed files
- plugins/pipeline-core/lib/human-guard-override.test.mjs: S2 (hardenKilledWriterStore + assertChildKilled, called from killedAuditWriter, killedAuditLockPublisher, killedAuditReclaimer) and S4 (heldLockCode per platform). 51 insertions, 5 deletions; every hunk confirmed with git diff before staging.
- Untracked, git-ignored, not committed: evidence/WIN-HGO-S-20261009/*.txt, evidence/dispatch-record-WIN-HGO-S-20261009.json, scratch/finalize-WIN-HGO-S.mjs, scratch/report-WIN-HGO-S-20261009.txt, scratch/commit-msg/WIN-HGO-S-20261009.txt.

4. Deliberately not changed
- All production files (forbidden). The script test file guard-human-override.test.mjs (no edit; S3 not reached). The recovery-guard exclusion case (left red, see above). Line 2137 (a git rev-parse show-toplevel comparison in the author-repair case) was not touched; that case is gated by S1, not S3. The foreign untracked files in specs/sprint-alfred-epic/evidence were not touched.

5. Deviations from spec
- The briefing asked for S1-S4; only S2 and S4 landed, because orientation consumed about 35 of 55 calls (the files are 6000+ lines and the work needed regions across five places) and the 80 % notice fired at call 44.
- S2 "injects the win32 private-state assurance": the child is a bare node -e process and publishAuditLock() calls safePrivateFile() with its defaults, so there is no injection seam. I used the repository's own T90 precedent instead (harden the store directory so created files inherit an owner-only DACL, assert status "secure"). That is a design choice inside the briefed latitude.
- GF-09-D: the record log carries only the opening entry and the final entry (the finalizer is the first and only run of that script; it was not dry-tested). The first capture attempt failed on a usage error (capture-evidence.mjs needs --label); one call wasted.
- The advisor tool was not consulted, because of the call budget.

6. Open items
- independent review: pending (only the Elephant may dispatch the Critic). PO acceptance pending. This is a closing-allowance handover, not a completed run.
- Next briefing must say: (a) capture-evidence.mjs needs --label <label> besides --out; (b) split the remainder into two dispatches: S1+S3 (pure edits; anchor by TEXT, not line numbers, because my commit shifted every later line by about +46), and a separate one for the recovery-guard exclusion case plus its confirmation (read the test body from its title, accept HGO-AUDIT-LOCK-AMBIGUOUS on win32 at the nested call if the assertions confirm the same live-owner design, keep the recovery-lock survival assertions); (c) give the exact edits to reduce orientation: S1 = add { skip: DIRECTORY_SYMLINK_SKIP } (constant already defined near the top of the lib test file) to the four tests "security and authority boundaries return typed recovery without an ambient bypass", "NVA-W4-01B: HGO-EXTERNAL-PROJECT-BOUNDARY discloses a bounded copy-safe rendering of the exact denied Bash command", "pipeline author repair binds one exact source root and action without State readiness", "NOVA-HGOELIG-4: an in-root symlink or hardlink attack is never reclassified as a cross-repository target"; S3 CROSSREPOGUIDANCE = wrap the git(...) results in join(...) at the two assert.equal(recorded.root, git(..., "--show-toplevel"), ...) lines of 1a and 1b (join is already imported and normalises separators natively; POSIX unchanged); (d) a budget of 55 is enough for S1+S3 plus one native and one WSL chunk only if orientation stays under about 15 calls.
